summary: The circular embedding conjecture (equivalently, the strong embedding conjecture) is now settled for cubic graphs and remains open for general 2-connected graphs. The cubic case follows from the July 2026 proof of the cycle double cover conjecture (OpenAI/GPT-5.6; exposition arXiv:2607.16356, Section 1) via the classical reduction in Jaeger's survey: for cubic graphs a cycle double cover and a closed 2-cell embedding are interchangeable. Earlier progress: Ellingham and Zha (2011) proved the orientable variant for 2-connected projective-planar cubic graphs, and Ghanbari and Sámal (2026) develop facial-diagram tools bounding singular edges in circular 2-cell embeddings. The general (non-cubic) case, and the orientable strengthening, are untouched by the new proof.

since_posted.title: A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition
since_posted.claim: The cycle double cover conjecture is now a theorem (proof announced by OpenAI in July 2026; Theorem 1 of this exposition). Since a cycle double cover of a cubic graph yields a strong (closed 2-cell) embedding -- the reduction recorded in Jaeger's survey -- the circular embedding conjecture now holds for all 2-connected cubic graphs. Section 1 states it explicitly: "Theorem 1 proves Conjecture 2 for cubic graphs". The conjecture remains open for general 2-connected graphs, and the embedding it produces need not be orientable.

since_posted.title: Orientable embeddings and orientable cycle double covers of projective-planar graphs
since_posted.venue: arXiv preprint (journal: European Journal of Combinatorics, 2011)
since_posted.claim: Proves that every 2-connected projective-planar cubic graph has a closed 2-cell (circular) embedding in some orientable surface, and that every 2-edge-connected projective-planar graph has an orientable cycle double cover, establishing the oriented circular embedding conjecture for this graph class.

since_posted.title: Facial diagrams and cycle double cover
since_posted.claim: Introduces a facial-diagram framework for circular 2-cell embeddings of cubic graphs, studies an edge-twisting operation that transforms one 2-cell embedding into another, and derives bounds on the number of singular edges, providing new tools for attacking the circular embedding / cycle double cover conjecture.

notes: Mohar (2009/2010, arXiv:0908.1933) showed that closed 2-cell embeddings may require surfaces of genus proportional to the order of the graph for some cubic graphs, disproving a minimum-genus folklore conjecture attributed to Tutte, but this does not disprove the circular embedding conjecture (which asks for existence on any surface). Ellingham and Zha (2015, arXiv:1501.06043) developed a partial-duality characterisation of closed 2-cell embeddings. A claim circulating in survey literature that 'any 2-connected graph without the Möbius 4-ladder as a minor has a closed 2-cell embedding' could not be traced to a verifiable source within the search budget. The ScienceDirect page for the Ellingham-Zha journal paper returned HTTP 403; the arXiv preprint was verified instead. 2026-09-06 update: the cycle double cover conjecture itself is now a theorem (OpenAI/GPT-5.6, July 2026; exposition arXiv:2607.16356). Because this conjecture implies CDC, the implication edge to opg:cycle_double_cover_conjecture in data/relations.json is now vacuous; the live content of this page is the non-cubic case, which the new proof does not reach (vertex splitting destroys the embedding).
